items.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase
items.stem: According to the latest forecast, the pattern of pressure changes near the coast ____ before dawn.
items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern takes the singular verb is; the intervening of-phrase does not change the subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: is agrees with the singular subject pattern.
distractor_rationales.B: The plural verb are incorrectly agrees with pressure or changes instead of pattern.
distractor_rationales.C: This is a nonfinite fragment and does not provide a finite main verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This repeats the subject and omits the required finite verb construction after the blank.

items.subtype: embedded question with statement word order
items.stem: The map archivist explained ____ during the survey.

options.A: where had the old boundary markers been moved
options.B: where the old boundary markers had been moved
options.D: where did the old boundary markers move

items.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: subject before the auxiliary, as in where the markers had been moved.

distractor_rationales.A: The auxiliary is inverted as in a direct question, so the embedded clause has the wrong word order.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the embedded question has the subject before the auxiliary.
distractor_rationales.C: The embedded clause is incomplete because it lacks a finite verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This uses direct-question inversion inside an embedded question.

items.subtype: non-restrictive relative clause with passive predicate
items.stem: The sandstone tablet, ____ during the excavation, is now displayed in the conservation laboratory.
items.answer_explanation: The non-restrictive relative clause needs which as its marker and the passive verb phrase was uncovered.

distractor_rationales.A: What cannot introduce this non-restrictive relative clause.
distractor_rationales.B: Uncovering is the wrong verb form for the required passive predicate.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: which introduces the clause and was uncovered is passive and finite.
distractor_rationales.D: The relative marker and a redundant subject pronoun duplicate the subject.

items.subtype: time clause introduced by when
items.stem: The telescope records extra images ____ the sky becomes clear after sunset.
items.answer_explanation: The time clause requires when followed by a subject and a finite verb: the sky becomes clear.

distractor_rationales.A: During is a preposition and cannot introduce the following finite clause.
distractor_rationales.B: The clause uses a nonfinite form instead of the required finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject and predicate are incorrectly ordered and the clause is not well formed.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: when introduces a complete time clause with subject and finite verb.

items.subtype: contrast connector before a noun phrase
items.stem: The alloy remains flexible ____ repeated cooling and heating.
items.answer_explanation: Despite correctly introduces the noun phrase repeated cooling and heating to express contrast.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: despite is followed directly by a noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Although must introduce a finite clause, not the noun phrase that follows.
distractor_rationales.C: In spite requires the preposition of before this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Despite does not take of; the extra preposition is unnecessary.

items.subtype: past perfect passive before a later past event
items.stem: By the time the survey team arrived, the mineral samples ____ in sealed containers.
items.answer_explanation: The earlier completed event requires past perfect, and the samples receive the action, so the form is had been labeled.

distractor_rationales.A: The participle is malformed; label must be in its past-participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: had been labeled is past perfect passive.
distractor_rationales.C: The active form incorrectly makes the samples perform the labeling.
distractor_rationales.D: The passive auxiliary is missing its required past participle.

items.subtype: causative verb with object plus predicate adjective
items.stem: The monitoring station's new filter made the river water ____ after heavy rainfall.
items.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare predicate adjective: made the water clearer.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: clearer is the adjective complement after the object river water.
distractor_rationales.B: Clearly is an adverb, not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.C: Make does not take to plus the infinitive in this object-complement pattern.
distractor_rationales.D: The -ing form does not function as the required adjective complement here.

items.subtype: reduced passive participial modifier
items.stem: ____ in shaded soil, the seeds germinated slowly after the spring rain.
items.answer_explanation: The seeds receive the action, so a reduced passive modifier uses the past participle planted.

distractor_rationales.A: Having planting is not a valid perfect participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: The active participle incorrectly presents the seeds as doing the planting.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: planted is a reduced passive modifier of the seeds.
distractor_rationales.D: Were planted is a finite clause fragment and cannot modify the subject in this position.

items.subtype: adjective plus enough plus to-infinitive result construction
items.stem: The detector was ____ to register faint signals from the distant star.
items.answer_explanation: Enough follows the adjective in the adjective + enough + to-infinitive construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Enough is placed before the adjective instead of after it.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: sensitive enough licenses the following to-infinitive.
distractor_rationales.C: So normally requires a that-clause for this result construction.
distractor_rationales.D: The following form is not the required to-infinitive construction.

items.subtype: parallel bare infinitives in a three-part list
items.stem: During fieldwork, the geologists had to ____ the slope, record the rock layers, and label the samples.
items.answer_explanation: Had to is followed by a bare infinitive, and measure is parallel with record and label.

distractor_rationales.A: The -ing form is not the bare infinitive required after had to.
distractor_rationales.B: A noun cannot be coordinated with the two verb forms in the list.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: measure is the bare infinitive parallel to record and label.
distractor_rationales.D: The added to creates to to measure after had to.

items.subtype: adjective order inside a complex noun phrase
items.stem: The museum displayed ____ from the coastal excavation.

options.B: a finely work small bronze bowl
options.C: a finely worked old small bronze bowl
options.D: a finely worked small bronze bowl

items.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely worked precedes the size adjective small, which precedes the material adjective bronze and the noun bowl.

distractor_rationales.A: The modifiers are ordered incorrectly around the participial adjective and material adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: Work is the wrong part-of-speech form; the participial modifier is worked.
distractor_rationales.C: The unnecessary adjective old adds an extraneous element to the planned noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the modifier order is finely worked, small, bronze, bowl.

items.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after only after
items.stem: Only after the glacier retreated ____ the researchers discover the buried lake.
items.answer_explanation: Fronted only after triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: did the researchers discover.

distractor_rationales.A: The inverted auxiliary lacks the required subject.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the auxiliary precedes the subject after fronted only after.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject remains before the auxiliary, so inversion is absent.
distractor_rationales.D: This is a nonfinite and incorrectly ordered fragment.

items.subtype: there plus be with a plural postposed noun phrase
items.stem: Near the wind-eroded ridge, ____ several narrow channels after the storm.
items.answer_explanation: The existential construction uses there, and the plural postposed noun channels requires were.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: there were agrees with the plural noun channels.
distractor_rationales.B: It is a referring pronoun and does not form the required existential construction.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular verb was does not agree with plural channels.

items.subtype: plural pronoun reference for a coordinated human subject
items.stem: The mentor and the apprentice recorded their measurements before ____ submitted the report.
items.answer_explanation: The coordinated subjects are plural, so the following subject pronoun is they.

distractor_rationales.A: He is singular and cannot refer to both the mentor and the apprentice.
distractor_rationales.B: Them is an object pronoun, not the subject of submitted.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: they is the plural subject pronoun for the two people.
distractor_rationales.D: Their is possessive and cannot function as the subject here.

items.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition
items.stem: The accuracy of the experiment depends on ____ of the instrument before each trial.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition on requires a noun phrase, and the noun calibration is the head of the phrase.

distractor_rationales.A: A verb phrase cannot serve as the required noun object of on in this construction.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun and adjective are in the wrong order.
distractor_rationales.C: The noun head calibration is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the careful calibration is a complete noun phrase after on.

items.subtype: singular head noun in an of-phrase subject
items.sentence: The calibration of the instruments record stable readings during each trial.

marked_parts.A: The calibration of the instruments record

items.answer_explanation: Calibration is the singular head of the subject noun phrase, so the main verb must be records.

items.subtype: adjective required before a plural head noun
items.sentence: The engineer selected several durability bearings for the test rig.
items.answer_explanation: The noun bearings needs an adjective modifier, so durable, not the noun durability, is required.

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect subordinate clause
items.sentence: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp, the keeper records the inspection details.

marked_parts.A: After the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp,

items.answer_explanation: The past perfect clause establishes a past time frame, so the main verb should be simple past recorded.

items.subtype: adjective-governed preposition in an interested-in phrase
items.sentence: The archivist was deeply interested on maps from the coastal archive.

marked_parts.D: on maps from the coastal archive.

items.answer_explanation: The established adjective-preposition collocation is interested in, not interested on.

items.subtype: gerund complements coordinated after a training preposition
items.sentence: The workshop focuses on carve wood and shaping clay for architectural models.
items.answer_explanation: The preposition on takes gerund complements, and carving must be parallel with shaping.

items.subtype: adjective complement after responsible for
items.sentence: The engineer is responsible to the mountain station's ventilation system.
items.answer_explanation: When responsible means having duty for something, it is followed by the preposition for.

items.subtype: subject relative pronoun for a human antecedent
items.sentence: The surveyor which mapped the village explained the boundary changes.
items.answer_explanation: The antecedent surveyor is a person and is the subject of mapped, so the relative marker should be who.

items.subtype: participial adjective before a material adjective in a noun phrase
items.sentence: The museum restored a bronze finely decorated vessel from the collection.
items.minimal_correction: bronze finely decorated vessel → finely decorated bronze vessel
items.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely decorated precedes the material adjective bronze in the noun phrase.

items.subtype: singular head noun with an of-phrase interrupter
items.sentence: The collection of oral histories contain vivid accounts of migration from the valley.

marked_parts.A: The collection of oral histories contain

items.answer_explanation: The singular head noun collection controls agreement; the plural noun histories is inside an of-phrase.

items.subtype: removal of a redundant coordinator after an although clause
items.sentence: Although the route was steep, but the hikers reached the summit before noon.
items.answer_explanation: Although already introduces the subordinate contrast clause, so the additional coordinator but is unnecessary.

items.subtype: passive transitive verb requiring a by-agent phrase
items.sentence: The manuscript was carefully restored the librarian last year.
items.minimal_correction: restored the librarian → restored by the librarian
items.answer_explanation: In the passive construction, the agent must be introduced by by: restored by the librarian.

items.subtype: past participle after a perfect auxiliary
items.sentence: The team has carefully prepared the samples that they have record.
items.answer_explanation: The auxiliary have requires the past participle recorded.

items.subtype: pronoun without an explicit antecedent
items.sentence: It was placed beside the research equipment after the technician finished.
items.answer_explanation: The sentence supplies no antecedent for It; an explicit noun such as The sensor is needed.

items.subtype: adjective required as a noun modifier after an article
items.sentence: The lecturer presented a scientifically overview of public water systems.
items.answer_explanation: The noun overview requires the adjective scientific as its modifier, not the adverb scientifically.

items.subtype: comparative adjective without a redundant more marker
items.sentence: The northern route is considerably more shorter than the southern route during winter.

marked_parts.C: more shorter than the southern route

items.answer_explanation: Shorter is already a comparative form, so the redundant more must be removed.

items.subtype: because clause rather than because-of before a finite clause
items.sentence: The plants grew slowly during the trial because of the soil remained unusually cold.

marked_parts.D: of the soil remained unusually cold.

items.minimal_correction: because of the soil remained unusually cold → because the soil remained unusually cold
items.answer_explanation: A finite clause follows because, whereas because of must be followed by a noun phrase.

items.subtype: there-be agreement with a plural postposed noun phrase
items.sentence: There is several balconies along the theater's upper gallery.
items.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun balconies requires the plural form are in the existential construction.

items.subtype: embedded why-question with statement word order
items.sentence: The analyst could not determine why did the values change after calibration.
items.minimal_correction: why did the values change → why the values changed
items.answer_explanation: The clause after determine is an embedded question and therefore uses statement order.

items.subtype: adjective-governed dependent-on preposition
items.sentence: The strength of the coating is dependent of temperature and humidity.
items.answer_explanation: The established collocation is dependent on, so of is the wrong preposition.

items.subtype: gerund coordination after recommends
items.sentence: The committee recommends mapping the district and to revise its zoning plan.
items.answer_explanation: The complements coordinated after recommends should be parallel gerund phrases: mapping and revising.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify a verb
items.sentence: The seedlings grew rapid under the controlled lamps.
items.answer_explanation: The verb grew requires the adverb rapidly to describe how the seedlings grew.

items.subtype: reduced passive modifier before a finite passive predicate
items.sentence: The panels, having built from recycled glass, were tested for strength.
items.minimal_correction: having built from recycled glass → built from recycled glass
items.answer_explanation: The panels receive the action, so the reduced modifier must be passive: built from recycled glass.

items.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect passive clause
items.sentence: After the bridge had been inspected, engineers approves the repair plan.

marked_parts.A: After the bridge had been inspected,

items.answer_explanation: The completed inspection places the following event in the past, so the main verb should be approved.

items.subtype: countable quantifier before a plural count noun
items.sentence: The questionnaire included much responses from first-year students.
items.answer_explanation: Responses is a plural count noun, so it requires the quantifier many rather than much.

items.subtype: adverb required to modify an adverb
items.sentence: The seedlings grew surprising quickly in the greenhouse.
items.answer_explanation: The word modifies the adverb quickly, so it must be the adverb surprisingly.
